item.title: New 3D model reveals how shadows reshape chemistry in stellar nurseries
item.description: How do young stars reshape the clouds from which they are born? A new high-resolution 3D model developed by an international team led by Dr Brandt Gaches from the University of Duisburg-Essen shows how the uneven structure of stellar nurseries creates shadows that alter their chemistry and influence the infrared emission observed by the James Webb Space Telescope. The model has now been published in Astronomy & Astrophysics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists discover cell division does more than make new cells: It helps reshape tissues
item.description: Every time a tissue grows or renews itself, cells must divide inside an already crowded environment. That creates a fundamental problem that scientists have not fully understood: How does a tightly packed sheet of cells make room for two daughter cells when there was once only one? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New details emerge in US investigations of Chinese-American scientists over China links
item.description: A US congressional committee has released details of investigations into dozens of researchers, many of them Chinese-American, revealing the scale of government scrutiny sweeping academia over alleged links to China. The documents – running to hundreds of pages – were released alongside a separate report by the House Select Committee on China. Titled “How to Stop China’s Theft of Taxpayer-Funded Research”, the report pushes back against arguments by universities and academic groups that tighter... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Sexual violence concepts launched online are spilling into the real world
item.description: Andrew Tate, a self-described misogynist and an online influencer with millions of followers, faces charges in several countries of allegedly causing physical harm, including rape and sex trafficking of women and girls. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New high-frequency method boosts 2D material readout for next-gen quantum computers
item.description: Quantum computers represent a next step in the fast-paced evolution of technology. Using quantum bits (qubits), they have the potential to run certain calculations exponentially faster than conventional computers. However, developing and fine-tuning quantum computers requires an enormous number of repetitive tests. To accelerate quantum technology development, we need a method that can read quantum states at ultrafast speeds. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Sunlight gives biodiesel byproduct a second life as hydrogen and valuable chemicals
item.description: Australian researchers and international collaborators have demonstrated a solar-driven approach to convert glycerol, a low-value byproduct of biodiesel production, into hydrogen and higher-value chemicals. Using advanced techniques at the Australian Synchrotron, they revealed how the catalyst changed while it was working. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A highway instead of a racetrack: Strong coupling of light and sound in an optical fiber
item.description: For the first time, scientists have achieved strong coupling between light and long-lived acoustic vibrations in an optical fiber. Optical fibers are used in both classical telecommunications and quantum communication and could serve not only as connections between computing nodes but also as quantum processors themselves in the future. The results, published in Nature Physics, pave the way for new technologies in quantum signal processing. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Infrared light overcomes mirror coating obstacle in gravitational wave detector upgrades
item.description: Researchers have developed and tested a new locking method for gravitational wave detectors that will advance the discovery of distant black holes and neutron stars colliding. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: First comprehensive Mars soil classification offers framework for exploration and future farming
item.description: A Ph.D. student at the University of Sydney has produced the first comprehensive classification system and map of Martian soils, creating a new framework that could help scientists compare landscapes across the Red Planet and identify promising locations for future exploration, habitation and food production. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Judging strangers' preferences may actually be easier when they're less like our own
item.description: Researchers already know that humans have a tendency to use egocentric anchoring—a cognitive bias in which people use their own preferences, beliefs and perspectives as a mental starting point (or anchor) to understand or predict what another person thinks, feels or prefers. This is not necessarily a sign of selfishness or self-importance, but a way for us to better understand others. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Essential oil sprays kill cockroaches on contact but offer little lasting control
item.description: A German cockroach races across a kitchen floor. Someone grabs a bottle of essential oil spray, soaks the insect and watches it die. The product worked, but a new University of Kentucky study suggests the larger infestation probably did not notice. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Names Stephen Cash Marshall Space Flight Center Director
item.description: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman has named Stephen Cash director of the agency’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, effective Monday, Oct. 19. Cash, a veteran NASA engineer and aerospace executive, returns to lead the center where he began his career more than four decades ago. “Marshall contributions to NASA’s missions are historic and it’s […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Invasive fire ants return to organic farms not treated for 14 months
item.description: Treatment on export-certified organic farms was paused in August 2025 after genetically modified ingredients were discovered in the baits used to treat nests. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Belief in change matters more than political anger when it comes to voting intentions, study suggests
item.description: With the 2026 midterm elections around the corner, voters may be feeling everything from excitement to fear. But how might anger motivate political activism and, ultimately, influence who turns out to vote? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Genetic evidence raises questions about settler-Indigenous relations in New France
item.description: A Université de Montréal–led research team has analyzed the genetic origins of human remains found in Old Montreal—and uncovered unexpected results. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Climate warming can slow how tree roots feed soil microbes
item.description: A plant's roots do much of their work out of sight, pulling in water and nutrients and holding the plant in place. That makes it hard to see how plants respond when conditions underground change, and how a warming climate affects them. New Dartmouth-led studies look at the strategies plants use below the surface to adapt and survive. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: About 2% of natural gas supplied to a Midwest city leaks into the atmosphere
item.description: Most natural gas leakage in Indianapolis likely originates from homes and other buildings, not exterior pipelines and large-scale distribution infrastructure that deliver the fossil fuel, according to Penn State researchers who assessed nearly a decade of data. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Submerged Archaeological Sites Study: Researchers map two underwater Aboriginal sites; stone moved 23 km
item.description: Archaeologists collaborated with Indigenous rangers to explore submerged sites off Murujuga in Western Australia. They uncovered artefacts and evidence of past human activity before rising sea levels altered the landscape. Two key locations highlighted interactions with freshwater resources and elevated terrains. The research involved several universities and emphasized the importance of Indigenous expertise in cultural heritage. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: New alloy design strategy combines strength and ductility by timing hardening mechanisms
item.description: Structural metals used in engineering projects are expected to have both high strength and high ductility: the ability to withstand heavy loads and deform before failure. Achieving both of these properties at the same time, however, is challenging. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Light and ultrasound reveal renewable routes to compounds for pharmaceutical research
item.description: Sustainable packaging is only the beginning. What a medicine is made from—and how its ingredients are produced—matters just as much. Yet the synthesis of compounds for pharmaceutical research can still depend on fossil feedstocks, high temperatures, strong oxidants and metals that raise costs and complicate purification. Two recently published studies from Colmenares' group at IPC PAS demonstrate that cleaner chemistry can begin at the level of a single chemical bond. The studies are published in the journal Ultrasonics Sonochemistry and Chemistry—A European Journal. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Edinburgh's historic Palm Houses reopen after a £23.5m restoration replaced 5,750 panes of glass
item.description: The Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh's Palm Houses have undergone extensive restorations costing £23.5 million over the past five years. Researchers carefully replaced all 5,750 glass panes to ensure they withstand harsh weather conditions. Following this work, nearly 600 rare plant specimens have been replanted in the glasshouses. The restoration enables continued conservation, education, and scientific discovery efforts related to endangered flora. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: World-record intensity in attosecond hard-X-ray pulses could unlock closer study of electrons in atoms and molecules
item.description: Researchers used the European XFEL to create X-ray flashes that were not only extremely short but also reached record intensity for this type of pulse. The researchers focused the X-rays to an area roughly 100,000 times smaller than the cross section of a typical human hair. This concentrated the X-ray light into a tiny but extremely powerful spot. The method could enable detailed studies of how electrons behave in atoms and molecules and, in the long term, could even allow researchers to control electrons during chemical reactions. The team has now published the results of the experiment… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Automated essay assessment can grade writing more accurately across topics, study finds
item.description: An artificial intelligence (AI) model can score English essays with improved accuracy across different writing topics, according to work published in the International Journal of Continuing Engineering Education and Life-Long Learning. The tool could help schools assess student work more efficiently while reducing inconsistencies in grading. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Spiny dogfish blood contains a hormone long thought absent in sharks
item.description: Cortisol is a hormone that helps humans and many other animals regulate their energy use and respond to changing conditions. For a long time, sharks and rays were believed to rely on a different steroid hormone for these functions, without producing cortisol themselves. Now, a new study of North Pacific spiny dogfish, a species of small shark, challenges this view. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Maxwell's demon learns to turn concealed information into usable energy for microscopic systems
item.description: Since its introduction more than 150 years ago, the thought-provoking idea of Maxwell's demon has profoundly shaped our understanding of the relationship between information and energy. Maxwell's demon is an imagined microscopic gatekeeper that exploits information at the microscopic scale to produce macroscopic work. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Finding their sense of direction: Cell movement helps tissues establish polarity
item.description: From the hairs on our arms to the microscopic sensory structures of the inner ear, many tissues in the body are built with a clear sense of direction. To build these structures throughout development, individual cells must establish which way they are facing—and coordinate that orientation with cells around them. If they get this wrong, tissues may fail to form, form improperly or fail to function. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Adaptive molecular convergence more common than previously thought, distant jellyfish relatives reveal
item.description: A new study has found that adaptive molecular convergence—the process by which distantly related or unrelated species evolve the same genomic changes—is not as rare as previously thought. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Glowing liquids could help protect products from counterfeiters using distinctive ultraviolet light signatures
item.description: Researchers at Nottingham Trent University have developed room-temperature liquids containing chemical elements that produce distinctive patterns of light. They say the materials could provide a flexible new approach to optical tagging and anti-counterfeiting, while being compatible with existing processing and printing technologies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What makes a place ready for radical innovation? Researchers say resident openness matters
item.description: Why do some cities embrace new technologies and business models while others are slower to take them up? Economic conditions, infrastructure and access to technology clearly matter. But a new study from the University of Amsterdam and the University of St Gallen suggests there is another factor that has received much less attention: the psychological openness of the local population. Regions where people are more open to new experiences and unfamiliar ideas are more likely to be early adopters of radical innovations, the study says. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A distant supercluster of galaxies points to self-interacting dark matter
item.description: Seven billion light-years from Earth, there is an unexpected cluster of galaxies. It has two regions in the process of colliding with each other with a combined mass of more than two quadrillion solar masses. Given its mass, the distant cluster has been nicknamed El Gordo, the Fat One. What makes it unusual is that it's extraordinarily large for that period of the universe. How did such a large supercluster form so early? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: No DREAM, fewer offspring: Protein complex may play key role in plant fertility
item.description: A protein complex known as DREAM that normally puts the brakes on genes may also be crucial for reproduction in plants, according to new research published in Science Advances. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA's Hubble spies spiral's edge
item.description: This NASA Hubble Space Telescope image features the edge-on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827, located roughly 37 million light-years away in the constellation Columba, the Dove. Hubble captured the image as part of a survey looking at 260 satellite galaxies around 22 Milky Way–like host galaxies within a radius of about 32 million light-years from Earth. Hubble has already observed 111 of these satellite galaxies. The remaining galaxies will take an additional 149 Hubble orbits, one orbit for each galaxy, to observe. Publicado también por: NASA. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Forecasting 'tipping points' with AI climate simulation
item.description: The writer Malcolm Gladwell popularized the term "tipping points" to refer to the moment when a trend or social behavior crosses a threshold and rapidly spreads everywhere. In physics, tipping points occur when systems—say, Earth's climate—reach an unstable point and topple over into a sea of change that is sometimes irreversible. Examples include global warming or the melting of polar ice caps. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Machine learning analysis of gene regulation reveals new dimension of biological variability
item.description: Changes in our genes affect health risks from heart disease to cancer, but how those genes are turned on and off is just as crucial to health. What's more, almost all genes occur as two copies—one from each parent—that aren't necessarily turned on and off in sync. When that differential gene regulation goes awry, it can cause serious health problems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Elon Musk unveils Tesla’s ‘flying’ car
item.description: Tesla CEO Elon Musk unveiled what he described as a “flying” car, equipped with thrusters, during a live-streamed event at his SpaceX rocket company’s facility on Thursday. Technical and regulatory challenges have so far prevented the much-hyped flying car sector from getting off the ground. Musk revealed his new Roadster sports car during a launch event at a SpaceX test facility in Texas. During the demo, which was live-streamed on Tesla’s X account, the car launched from a steep steel ramp and... Publicado también por: Phys.org. Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse

item.title: 'Excess oxygen' stored in deep Earth magma may help explain how Earth's atmosphere became oxygen-rich
item.description: A research team has found that molten rock can carry more oxygen than its chemical composition would seem to allow. Their study is published in National Science Review. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ancient fungus unlocks secret support system in major food crops that could transform farming practices
item.description: Arabidopsis thaliana, a small flowering mustard plant used worldwide as the primary genetic model in plant biology, was long believed incapable of forming relationships with underground fungal networks. New research published in Current Biology led by professor Katie Field demonstrates for the first time that it can establish a fully functional, resource-sharing partnership with an ancient soil fungus known as a Mucoromycotina fine root endophyte (MFRE). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Wind emerges as overlooked factor in ecosystems' carbon uptake and water loss
item.description: Wind does more than sway trees. It also plays an important role in determining an ecosystem's water-use efficiency—defined as the amount of carbon an ecosystem absorbs per unit of water lost. Water-use efficiency is an important measure of how ecosystems balance growth and water availability. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA satellites observe historic 2026 El Niño
item.description: A phenomenon rarer than a solar eclipse and more powerful than any single storm system is unfolding this fall, and NASA is tracking it closely. El Niño is a natural climate pattern that emerges roughly every two to seven years marked by warmer-than-normal water temperatures in parts of the equatorial Pacific. NASA scientists are keeping […] Publicado también por: NASA. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Remote work made these colleagues more open with each other, not less
item.description: If you need to participate in video meetings for work, you've probably experienced more than one disruption, whether it's kids darting around or home renovation noise. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI designs working molecular scissors that recognize and cut selected protein targets
item.description: Proteases are naturally occurring enzymes that break down proteins into peptides and even single amino acids. They are useful in medicine and industrial processes, where they clean tissue, digest waste and help in the manufacture of everyday products. Now scientists have used artificial intelligence to design new versions from scratch. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Artemis II Heat Shield After Splashdown
item.description: Shortly after NASA’s Artemis II mission splashed down on April 10, 2026, U.S. Navy divers captured underwater imagery of the Orion spacecraft’s heat shield. In the months after, the agency measured whether the thermal protection system effectively safeguarded the crew and Orion systems as the spacecraft reentered Earth’s atmosphere. This rigorous analysis confirmed that the […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: The artisanal miners behind Nigeria’s lithium boom
item.description: Nasarawa is at the heart of Nigeria’s lithium boom, where artisanal miners hope to benefit from the clean energy race. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.title: Elon Musk unveils Tesla's 'flying' car
item.description: Tesla CEO Elon Musk unveiled what he described as a "flying" car, equipped with thrusters, during a livestreamed event at his SpaceX rocket company's facility on Thursday. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Matching wastewater treatment to local demand could help China tackle water scarcity
item.description: Wastewater reclamation is increasingly regarded as an alternative water source to mitigate water scarcity in China. However, expanding wastewater treatment capacity alone may not be enough to ease this scarcity, since wastewater supply, treatment facilities and reuse demand are not always geographically aligned. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: One-step rapid syphilis test uses layered nanoparticles to detect infection earlier
item.description: Penicillin has cured syphilis cases since 1943, but symptoms of the sexually transmitted infection, known as "the great imitator," mimic many other diseases and can come and go without treatment while the infection keeps causing harm. If it remains undetected, it can spread to partners and to babies during pregnancy, causing lifelong effects. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Can social media bans protect young people's mental health? Early research suggests that bans aren't the answer
item.description: The year 2026 has been an expensive one for social media platforms. Since March, YouTube and Meta, the parent company of Instagram and Facebook, have settled or paid out in multiple lawsuits totaling more than $17 billion for allegedly acting negligently, deliberately designing their platforms to hook kids and misleading the public about safety and privacy. If these suits are any indication of how states and the public are starting to view social media platforms, more may follow. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Physics-guided AI reconstructs hidden patterns inside ultrathin magnets from external fields
item.description: To build faster and more energy-efficient computers, researchers need to understand nanoscale magnetic materials. But looking inside these tiny magnets is surprisingly difficult: Modern microscopes only measure the magnetic field outside the material, not the magnetic pattern inside. Because many different internal patterns can produce the exact same field, working backwards has long been a challenge. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Putting wood security on the global agenda: Researchers outline 20 core challenges
item.description: A study led by the Centre for Global Wood Security formally defines the concept of global wood security and identifies the 20 greatest challenges to wood security in the 21st century. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mailchimp’s founders turned a side project into a $12 billion business without outside funding
item.description: Originating from humble beginnings, Mailchimp evolved within two decades from a small business tool to a powerhouse in the marketing industry. Launched by The Rocket Science Group's Ben Chestnut and Dan Kurzius, it caught the attention of Intuit, who acquired it for around $12 billion in 2021. With a sharp focus on customer-centric innovation and maintaining independence, Mailchimp solidified its status as a leader in global digital marketing. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: AI reveals a shared language guiding cell development
item.description: As an embryo develops from a small cluster of stem cells, those once "blank slate" cells begin to take on more specialized roles like brain, liver or muscle cells and organize themselves into three-dimensional structures such as tissues and organs. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: When schools fail to act, weight-based bullying can continue
item.description: Young people who experience bullying because of their weight feel that their schools do not take the problem seriously enough. In some cases, they change their own behavior to avoid harassment, according to a new study from Lund University. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Could your plastic film packaging serve a purpose? We won't know until recycling laws change
item.description: From the clear covering on your microwave meal to the flimsy bread bag lying on the kitchen counter, plastic film is notoriously tricky to recycle. But what if those annoying bits of plastic waste could be put to better use? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The same immune cells play opposing roles in tissue regeneration's balancing act
item.description: In a study of fingertip regeneration, a team led by JAX senior research scientist James Godwin found that some immune cells in mice can attack and kill cells needed to rebuild bone, while a subset of those same immune cells can protect the bone-making cells and allow regeneration to continue. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New water safety rapid testing method cuts time to results from six hours to 30 minutes
item.description: FIU researchers have developed a faster, more efficient method to detect forever chemicals in the water system, cutting the testing time from over six hours to just 30 minutes. These findings, which could enhance how water safety is monitored, were published in the Journal of Chromatography A. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Spain sizzles in hottest September on record: Weather agency
item.description: Mainland Spain sizzled in its warmest September since records began in 1961, with exceptional heat effectively making it another summer month, national weather agency AEMET said on Friday. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Forecasting air drag with deep learning helps predict when uncontrolled satellites and rocket stages fall to Earth
item.description: On May 10, 2025, a spacecraft built in the Soviet Union to land on Venus came home. Launched in 1972, Cosmos-482 was stranded by a failed upper stage of its rocket and circled Earth for 53 years. In its last days, several space agencies and research groups forecasted when it would fall, and therefore where. Roscosmos later reported that it came down in the Indian Ocean, west of Jakarta. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: I Am Artemis: Allison Mjoen
item.description: As the supercooled propellant flowed into the core stage, and NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket roared to life, Allison Mjoen and her family watched with awe and pride. Mjoen, NASA’s operations manager for the agency’s Exploration Ground Systems Program, helped shape the systems and ground operations that will one day send humans back to […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Jason Costa

item.title: Fully automated testing of bulk metals paves the way for AI-driven materials development
item.description: Developing stronger and tougher structural metals such as steel requires exploring an enormous range of processing conditions. Even for the same alloy composition, heat treatment can dramatically change the material's microstructure and mechanical properties. If there were a way to automate the process, we could pinpoint ideal conditions much more efficiently. However, experiments on bulk metallic materials are difficult to automate because they require handling solid specimens and integrating large, specialized equipment. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Even or odd numbers: A single molecule makes all the difference in the quantum world
item.description: The researchers in the Quantum Detection Microscopy group at CIC nanoGUNE, in collaboration with chemists at CiQUS of the University of Santiago de Compostela, have demonstrated that adding or removing a single molecule from a quantum chain can fundamentally change its interaction with a superconductor. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Han pillado a una flota de agentes de IA rebeldes campando por internet. Por primera vez, han sido creados y activados en China
item.description: Por primera vez, unos investigadores especializados en ciberseguridad han capturado a un grupo de agentes de IA autónomos merodeando por internet que habían sido desplegados desde infraestructura china. Durante diez días, los agentes bombardearon Amap, el servicio de mapas de Alibaba, con miles de intentos para extraer datos a los que no se suponía que debían poder acceder. El equipo detrás del descubrimiento, que trabajaba desde un hackathon, afirma que el tráfico provenía de Tencent Cloud. Agentes de IA locos . En los últimos meses hemos conocido cómo grupos de agentes de IA de empresas… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Vallejo

item.title: Fraudulent paper mills may be manipulating scientific citations and amplifying unreliable findings
item.description: The likely manipulation of citation numbers by research paper mills in high-impact cancer journals has been uncovered by an international team of academic researchers. Their findings point to an organized campaign to inflate citations on paper mill–produced journal articles published in established molecular oncology journals. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Kids and teens are going to AI chatbots for advice. How can parents make sure this is safe?
item.description: Last week, Australian Federal Police Commissioner Krissy Barrett warned artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are not a sufficient replacement for human support for children. The comment was in response to a recent Adelaide University study that found more than one in three Australian children turn to AI chatbots for support when they are sexually victimized online or otherwise tell nobody at all. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The force behind our strength: How mechanical processes regulate muscle development
item.description: Skeletal muscles grow and regenerate as individual precursor cells—called myoblasts—fuse into long fibers from which mature muscle fibers develop. How they coordinate this process and form functional muscles is not yet fully understood. A research team at the Max-Planck-Zentrum für Physik und Medizin (MPZPM) has now shown that mechanical stress influences the fusion of muscle cells. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI and wastewater DNA-based mapping help identify sewer pipes at risk of corrosion
item.description: Underground sewers that safely manage wastewater are essential to modern cities. However, since they are buried underground and difficult to access, their condition can be hard to monitor. Traditional camera inspections are costly and time-consuming, but we need regular inspections so aging pipes do not continue to deteriorate until they reach a breaking point. When damaged pipes leak, they can pose serious risks to public health by contaminating surrounding water, while more severe failures can even damage infrastructure above them, causing sinkholes in city streets. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Shredded star reveals a massive black hole wandering far from its galaxy's center
item.description: Astronomers have discovered a star being torn apart by a massive black hole more than 1,000 parsecs from the center of its host galaxy. The tidal disruption event, TDE 2023mfm, was first discovered by ZTF and then studied with a wide range of telescopes, including Keck, Lick, Hubble, Swift, Chandra, XMM-Newton and the VLA. The discovery paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 28. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What land crabs reveal about evolution's repeats
item.description: How can bodies adapt to survive environments completely different from the ones they evolved for? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Molecular fingerprints reveal how human activities alter water systems worldwide
item.description: A Florida State University–led review shows how ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry can help researchers identify the molecular fingerprints of human activity in water systems around the world. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Real-time nanoscale imaging reveals differences in antibody access to cancer-linked proteins on tiny vesicles
item.description: Researchers at the Nano Life Science Institute (WPI-NanoLSI) at Kanazawa University have developed a way to observe how antibodies interact with a cancer-related protein carried on tiny membrane-bound vesicles released by cells. Using high-speed atomic force microscopy, they found that measuring how much of the protein is present does not necessarily show how accessible it is to antibodies. The findings reported in the journal Small Methods provide a new way to investigate differences between individual cancer-derived vesicles although further research is needed before the approach can be… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: USC scientists discover how to create a never-ending supply of cancer-fighting cells
item.description: USC scientists have discovered a way to create a potentially renewable supply of genetically engineered immune cells that can attack cancer and strengthen the body's natural defenses. By growing and modifying immature immune cells rather than mature ones, researchers developed a system that can continuously produce tumor-fighting cells inside the body. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA’s Hubble Spies Spiral’s Edge
item.description: This NASA Hubble Space Telescope image features the edge-on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827, located roughly 37 million light-years away in the constellation Columba, the Dove. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Owners who spend more time close to their cats tend to have more positive moods
item.description: Many owners will enthusiastically attest that their cat has improved their quality of life. Some studies support this common claim that caring for a feline friend has positive effects on human health and well-being. However, the evidence is inconsistent, and other studies have even reported possible negative effects of cat ownership. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The uranium cubes that exposed Nazi Germany’s nuclear failure
item.description: Scientists investigating Nazi Germany's secret nuclear program have uncovered evidence that its final experimental reactor was nowhere near as close to working as previously claimed. Analysis of surviving uranium cubes and wartime documents reveals that Germany lacked the enormous quantities of uranium and heavy water needed to make its reactor operational. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Exchange rates react immediately to the threat of tariffs
item.description: Exchange rates are more than just abstract numbers. They determine the value of a Mexican peso, the cost of a German car in the U.S. and whether an Argentine farmer can repay his debts. Jantke de Boer, junior professor of international monetary macroeconomics at Ruhr University Bochum, has examined how expectations of future protectionist measures influence exchange rates. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tiny molecular changes, big microparticle deformation
item.description: Materials that change their shape upon exposure to light are attracting growing interest in applications such as soft robotics, microscale actuators and smart materials. However, the connection between molecular-level structural changes and larger-scale deformation remains incompletely understood. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: La NASA ofrece 150.000 dólares a quien evite que los astronautas se conviertan en “condensadores de alto voltaje” en la Luna
item.description: Los humanos ya han caminado sobre la Luna, pero la verdad es que es una suerte que no hubiese incidentes, ya que no se estudiaron a fondo algunos factores que podrían haber sido peligrosos . Por ejemplo, la posibilidad de convertirse en condensadores de alto voltaje e incendiar sus propias naves. Suena aterrador, básicamente porque lo es. Por eso, la NASA ha ofrecido 150.000 dólares a la persona o empresa que le ofrezca la mejor solución a este problema de cara a los próximos viajes de astronautas a nuestro satélite. Saltan chispas. Cuando los astronautas caminen sobre la Luna, pueden… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Sorry, Darwin: Chinese fossil shows that not all early birds evolved to fly
item.description: Chinese scientists have unearthed a fossil of the earliest known flightless bird, offering compelling evidence that not all early birds evolved to take to the skies. The discovery could also challenge long-held assumptions – including ideas dating back to evolutionary theorist Charles Darwin – that flightlessness in birds arose only as a secondary adaptation after earlier species had mastered flight. The 150 million-year-old fossil of the Late Jurassic avialan Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis found in... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Bela

item.title: Why exposure to firearm suicide may not mean safer gun storage
item.description: Knowing someone who died by firearm suicide is associated with greater recognition of suicide risk, but may not lead to safer storage practices, according to a Rutgers study published in Psychiatry Research. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Solving the gallium anomaly: New calculation may explain neutrino shortfall without invoking new particles
item.description: Glimpses of the "gallium anomaly" were first seen in the mid-1990s, but it was first clearly discovered and stated in 2007 by neutrino physicist Carlo Giunti of Italy. The problem is simple to state but potentially very important: about 20% fewer electron neutrinos were seen to be captured by gallium nuclei than expected. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Yale scientists discover how stress changes the brain to make memories stronger
item.description: Yale scientists have uncovered how the stress hormone cortisol helps the brain turn emotional experiences into stronger, longer-lasting memories. The discovery reveals that stress can reshape communication between brain networks involved in emotion and memory, potentially explaining why certain moments are so difficult to forget. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: "How long can we live without oxygen, but we stayed inside our mother's womb for 9 months?"
item.description: "How long can we live without oxygen, but we stayed inside our mother's womb for 9 months?" We didn't breathe air, but we got oxygen through the umbilical cord from our mother's blood. So we were never really without oxygen Tito AR "How long can we live without oxygen, but we stayed inside our mother's womb for 9 months?" We didn't breathe air, but we got oxygen through the umbilical cord from… Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Changing how you think about time could help you accomplish year-end goals: Q&A
item.description: The way time is described can shape everything from our motivation to our decision-making, according to new research from behavioral scientist Dr. Deepak Sirwani, an assistant professor at the UBC Sauder School of Business. The study is published in the Journal of Marketing Research. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: The pioneering reusable upper stage for Stoke Space's Nova rocket ships out for testing. Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Clark

item.title: Transferable chemical prediction approach may help reduce trial and error
item.description: Chemical predictions can help prevent unwanted reactions or improve the efficacy of industrial processes, among other applications, but predicting how chemicals interact can be costly and time-consuming—especially because chemicals may behave differently from one environment to another. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Astronomers discover a strange universal rule behind black hole eruptions
item.description: Scientists have discovered that black holes of vastly different sizes appear to launch powerful jets according to the same universal rule. The breakthrough could explain why some black holes suddenly erupt years after devouring a star and help astronomers predict when these spectacular outbursts will happen. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover a plastic-eating “Pac-Man” enzyme with a surprising secret
item.description: Scientists have discovered a remarkable “Pac-Man enzyme” that helps bacteria devour certain types of plastic and may offer new hope in the fight against plastic pollution. Researchers found that several biodegradable plastics completely broke down in soil within about a year, while conventional plastic remained largely unchanged. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Resistance to change has 12 different drivers, new measurement tool reveals
item.description: Almost all change is difficult: adapting your lifestyle, a reorganization at work, or starting to use gender-neutral language. When behavioral change is required, resistance is therefore often encountered. As a result, it can sometimes take a long time for a change to be accepted—and sometimes it doesn't happen at all. It is therefore important to understand where that resistance comes from, according to Radboud University communication scientist Marieke Fransen. Fransen and her colleagues investigated this and identified 12 reasons. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Blue Origin is going all in on the New Glenn rocket
item.description: The infrastructure is designed to support multiple flights per week by the end of the decade. Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Eric Berger

item.title: UN chief says ‘subsidising fossil fuels is subsidising suicide’
item.description: The United Nations says that for every dollar invested in protecting or restoring nature, about $30 still goes into activities that degrade it. Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: Winter sea ice loss may be underestimated, ancient clues from a warmer Arctic suggest
item.description: Future Arctic winter sea ice is likely to shrink by around 1 million square kilometers (386,000 square miles) more than previously thought, after researchers used clues from a warm period 6,000 years ago to improve the reliability of climate models. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Earth from Space: West Antarctica
item.description: Image: This image over part of West Antarctica was captured by Copernicus Sentinel-3 on 30 September 2026. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: Tesla unveils car that can drive upside down and jump through the air
item.description: Tesla has unveiled an electric car that can drive upside down and use rocket-like thrusters to jump and turn mid-air. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.title: All those Commando war stories I read.
item.description: All those Commando war stories I read. Sudeep Sarkar Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: NASA captures strange waves high above Hurricane Simon
item.description: As Hurricane Simon unleashed destructive winds and flooding along Mexico’s coast, NASA satellites captured an extraordinary sight: massive atmospheric waves rippling high above the storm. The rare images reveal how powerful hurricanes can disturb the upper atmosphere, creating patterns that are usually invisible from space. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Performance under pressure: A new perspective on why we fail—or rise to the occasion
item.description: The decisive penalty kick in a final, match point in tennis or the last attempt in a competition: When a lot is at stake, even a well-practiced performance can suddenly break down. Yet pressure does not necessarily impair performance. Some people perform at their best precisely in the moments that matter most. Existing accounts can only partly explain why. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: PLATO, el telescopio europeo con 26 ojos que quiere encontrar por fin una segunda Tierra
item.description: Desde que comenzaron a buscarse exoplanetas en 1992, se han documentado más de 6.000 , de los cuales apenas un centenar pueden considerarse similares a la Tierra. Cuando hablamos de planetas parecidos al nuestro, normalmente nos referimos a su morfología rocosa o al tamaño, no demasiado alejado del terrestre. Sin embargo, si nos proponemos buscar una Tierra 2, sería ideal que su órbita sea más o menos de un año. Es decir, que tarde en girar alrededor de su estrella el mismo tiempo que tarda la Tierra en dar una vuelta completa al Sol. Eso es más difícil de encontrar con los telescopios… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: A protein that fuels cancer could also be the key to fighting it
item.description: Scientists have discovered how to turn a protein that normally fuels cancer growth into a weapon against it. By activating PPARD in immune cells, researchers made them better at burning fat and attacking tumors, slowing or stopping cancer growth in laboratory experiments. The approach showed promise against colorectal, breast, and ovarian cancers, as well as melanoma. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A quantum highway just one atom high could transform superconductors
item.description: Scientists discovered that atomic steps just one atom high can guide quantum vortices through superconductors, making them move more than 1,000 times more easily in one direction than another. This remarkable control over quantum motion could lead to a new generation of ultra-efficient superconducting electronics. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 16 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. To view this […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: “Crawzilla” was huge. Then scientists found an even bigger crayfish
item.description: A nationwide search for giant crayfish uncovered a record-breaking Tennessee specimen and a surprising mystery about how big these freshwater creatures can grow. Scientists found that North American crayfish seem to hit a biological size limit, possibly because of their muscles or protective shells. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: First in-depth map of 'forever chemicals' in the Finger Lakes created
item.description: In 2023, professor Damian Helbling was getting a lot of calls and emails from local residents. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) had just announced regulations to limit per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)—some of which have been linked to cancers and other negative health effects—in drinking water. Ithacans and others in the region wanted to know about levels in the ponds, lakes, streams and creeks in their proverbial backyards. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Endangered species in Canada face extensive delays receiving protection
item.description: For more than 20 years, Canada's Species at Risk Act (SARA) has protected wildlife that are at risk of being lost from Canadian lands and waters. Once a species is listed as extirpated, endangered or threatened under the act, it becomes illegal to kill, harm or capture it or damage its residences. Its critical habitat must also be protected, at least on federal land. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A rare family of barn owls moved into Manhattan's Upper West Side. New Yorkers are captivated
item.description: Manhattan's Upper West Side has been reveling in the company of its latest celebrities: A family of barn owls nested in a water tower atop a building near Central Park. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Antarctica’s sea ice has undergone a stunning reversal
item.description: Antarctic sea ice reached its third-lowest winter maximum in 2026, extending a remarkable decline that began after years of record-breaking growth. Scientists are investigating whether the dramatic reversal signals a long-term shift in Antarctica's frozen landscape. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Can extra weight weigh on your dog's brain?
item.description: Scientists have learned a lot about what happens to the human body as we age. But there's still much to learn about how other species age, including dogs. Even carrying extra weight could affect a dog's cognitive health. Alexandra Genualdi, a student at Oklahoma State University who presented her research in September at the American Physiological Society's 2026 Comparative Physiology conference in Orlando, talks about her efforts to learn more. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: "Yo te daré nietos": familias israelíes usan el esperma póstumo de sus hijos para tener descendencia
item.description: A raíz del ataque de Hamás de 2023, una norma temporal de emergencia facilita que padres, pero también parejas, extraigan el semen de los cadáveres de sus seres queridos sin una orden judicial. El uso del material genético aún requiere el permiso de los tribunales de familia. No obstante, lo que antes era una práctica casi anecdótica, hoy se ha convertido en política de Estado y, en tres años, 21 civiles y 250 soldados muertos han pasado por este proceso. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: Janira Gómez Muñoz

item.title: Scientists discover how exercise reverses muscle aging
item.description: Scientists have uncovered a hidden biological mechanism that helps explain how exercise can reverse some of the damage caused by muscle aging. The key is a gene called DEAF1, which becomes overactive with age and interferes with the muscles’ ability to clear damaged proteins and repair themselves. Exercise can help restore this balance, allowing older muscles to rebuild and regain strength, although the benefits may diminish when the system becomes too disrupted. Fuente: ScienceDaily.
